title: Kanpur Man Dies After Being Dragged 1.5 km on Car Roof, Family Alleges Murder
excerpt: Biru Singh Bhadauria, 37, died in Kanpur after an incident his family says involved being hit by a car, placed on its roof with his hands trapped in the windows and driven for 1.5 km. Police say the complaint they received described a hit by an unidentified vehicle, and the investigation is under way.
body:
• Biru Singh Bhadauria, 37, a food-products salesman from Arra in Kanpur, died on Wednesday after an incident on the night of October 20, following a Dussehra fair.
  • His family alleges that five men, including two he had a dispute with, hit him with a car, assaulted him, placed him on the roof with his hands trapped between the front windows, and drove about 1.5 km before he was thrown off and run over.
  • Police give a narrower account so far: ACP Abhishek Rahul said the written complaint received on October 21 stated Bhadauria died after being hit by an unidentified vehicle.
  • The family says more than 12 CCTV cameras cover the area and two clips are available; police say they are examining the footage and further action will follow the facts the probe establishes.

A 37-year-old man died in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, after he was allegedly dragged for about 1.5 kilometres on the roof of a moving car with his hands trapped in its windows, in an incident his family has alleged was murder and police are investigating.

The man, Biru Singh Bhadauria, worked as a salesman for a food products company and lived in Arra, Kanpur. He was returning home after attending a Dussehra fair at about 10:30 pm on October 20 when, his family alleges, he was intercepted by a group of men with whom he had an earlier dispute.

The Family's Account

According to his father, Ram Shankar Singh, the men — including Rajveer and Mewalal, with three associates — stopped Bhadauria and assaulted him. When he tried to escape, they allegedly hit him with the car, placed him on its roof and trapped both his hands between the front windows, then drove at high speed for about 1.5 km. The family alleges his hands were then loosened, throwing him onto the road, and that the car ran over him before the men fled.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2113107929465549106

Passersby informed the family and police. Bhadauria was taken to a private hospital and referred to Hallet Hospital, where doctors declared him dead at about 3 pm on Wednesday. His family said his fingers were badly crushed and his body carried multiple injuries. He leaves three children.

What Police Say

The police account is more limited, and the gap between the two versions is now the centre of the case. ACP Abhishek Rahul said that on October 21, complainant Pradeep Shukla submitted a written complaint at Hanumant Vihar police station stating that Bhadauria died after being hit by an unidentified vehicle, according to the IANS report carried by HiIndia. A case has been registered on the family's complaint and the matter is under investigation, with legal action to follow the facts established, he said.

The family says the sequence was captured by more than 12 CCTV cameras in the area, that two clips are reportedly available, and that a video purporting to show the incident has circulated on social media. Police are examining the footage. The family has protested at the police station demanding strict action and rejecting any suggestion that the death was an accident, Nation Press reported.

What Happens Next

The CCTV record should settle the central dispute: whether Bhadauria was carried on the roof of an identified car, as his family alleges, or struck by an unidentified vehicle, as the initial complaint described. No arrests had been reported in the accounts published on Thursday. The Videshi will update this story as police name suspects or release findings from the footage.
